_source: ERC Guidelines 2025, Adult Basic Life Support, as summarised in docs/BLS.md. The instructor answers CPR questions from these facts only. Review by qualified BLS instructors before curricular use.
facts: Safety first: before approaching, check for dangers to yourself and the person, such as traffic, fire, electricity, gas or water.
Check for a response: speak loudly to the person and gently tap or shake the shoulders.
If the person does not respond, call emergency services on 112 at once, before checking breathing (new in 2025).
If someone else is there, ask them by name to call 112 and to fetch an AED, while you stay with the person. If you are alone, call 112 yourself, put the phone on speaker and stay with the person.
Open the airway with head tilt and chin lift, then look, listen and feel for normal breathing for no more than ten seconds.
Gasping, slow, laboured or noisy breathing is not normal breathing. If in doubt, act as if breathing is not normal and start CPR.

Compressions: in the centre of the chest, on the lower half of the breastbone, 100 to 120 per minute, 5 to 6 cm deep, letting the chest come fully back up after each one, with as few pauses as possible.
For an adult, give 30 compressions, then 2 rescue breaths, and repeat. If you cannot or will not give rescue breaths, give continuous compressions.

Use an AED as soon as one is available; no set number of compressions is needed first. Follow its spoken prompts. Nobody touches the person during analysis and shock. Restart CPR straight after a shock, or after the AED advises no shock.
With two or more helpers, compressions continue while the AED pads are put on and pause only for analysis and shock.
Keep going until emergency services take over, or the person wakes up, moves, opens the eyes and breathes normally.
